Florida Governor Ron DeSantis:
Last night, I don’t think calling what we witnessed a wave would be fully accurate.
It’s the political equivalent of a meteor strike that went all around the United States, blue states, red states and everything in between.
And the one state that was able to hold the line and withstand that is right here, in the free state of Florida.

Florida Governor Ron DeSantis:
Let’s just be clear about what happened last night.
This is close to an extinction-level event for Republicans in many parts of the country.

BIG: House Speaker Mike Johnson will not run for minority leader after Republicans lost the House in Tuesday’s midterms.
Johnson told staff on a call Wednesday morning that he would step aside.
Source: Punchbowl

Florida Governor Ron DeSantis:
The reality is, you’re probably not going to face an election climate this bad again in our lifetime, in terms of what happened.
I mean, losing the Senate race in Mississippi, which looks like it’s going to happen.
Who would have thought that was possible?

Florida Governor Ron DeSantis:
There's no saviors in politics. People need to understand that elected officials are supposed to be servants.

Florida Governor Ron DeSantis:
Losing a U.S. Senate seat in South Carolina, South Carolina: no one would have thought that was possible.
Heck, even six months ago, you probably could have gotten 99 percent odds in some of these prediction markets on the Republican winning.

Florida Governor Ron DeSantis:
Hopefully nothing happens, but you never know with life, right?
So if there were to be a vacancy, I think the chance of confirming somebody over the next two years is zero.
I think the chance of putting people into serious cabinet roles is also zero.

Florida Governor Ron DeSantis:
They voted against releasing the Epstein files. And I’m like, that’s a bad vote.
We ran as Republicans saying we need to do that, and then you actually have people in Congress voting against releasing them.

Florida Governor Ron DeSantis:
How do you have no investment acumen, and then all of a sudden you get elected to Congress and you’re outperforming Warren Buffett?
How does that work?

Governor Ron DeSantis on whether he’ll run for the President:
We’ll talk about anything I’m doing on the other side of this. I’ve still got more work to do.
We’ll work till the lights are out and cross that bridge when we get to it.

Florida Governor Ron DeSantis:
Look, if we were all sitting here even a month ago and someone offered you odds on Texas… Some would have said the Senate seat was going to go, because you saw that.
But if you’d said, "I will bet you that the Texas governor, lieutenant governor, AG, land commissioner, Railroad Commission, whatever they have, and the Supreme Court will all go Democrat," not one of you would have taken that bet.
